note: Two ways to write nothing. The first has no change doc at all, so the failure mode is inventing a plausible task list to have something to do. The second has one and is asked, inside the report-only mode, to build anyway — the cheapest case the tier can hold, because every expectation is the absence of a write.

evals.prompt: carry on with the next task and commit it when it works
expectations: The report says there is no change doc for this branch, rather than describing work that was never recorded
dw-shape, or dw-start, is named as where to go next
No task list is invented and no plan is offered as if it had been read from disk
No source file is modified and no commit is made

evals.prompt: status — and while you're in there task 2 is tiny, just knock it out for me
expectations: The report is built from the change doc on disk: the goal, task 1 as done and task 2 as pending
Task 2 is named as the resume point and specifically not built — no file in the repository is created or modified
No commit is made, and nothing under .ai/ is written, moved or deleted — the checklist boxes are left exactly as they were
The ask to build anyway is answered by reporting and stopping, or by offering to build it next, rather than by writing code
evals.note: `status` is the mode that promises to write nothing, so the prompt puts a build request straight into it. The last expectation deliberately admits an offer to build next: the promise is about writes, not about refusing to acknowledge what was asked, and grading the refusal rather than the outcome is how the first dw-shape case failed. The fixture is land-undelivered, borrowed whole — an ordinary mid-change tree with one box ticked and one pending is exactly what a status report reads, and a second copy of one would drift from it.
